dedupe_keys.name: how power outages affect health in new york city 2003 blackout and local outages

description: This NYC Health Department data story shows how power outages harm health in New York City. It compares observed with predicted hospitalisations and deaths around the blackout of 14 August 2003, when power was lost citywide on a day in the 90s Fahrenheit, and finds spikes in respiratory hospitalisations and deaths; studies of local outages in July 1999 and July 2006 found more respiratory and kidney hospitalisations and higher mortality. It adds that 7.6% of households citywide, and nearly 17% in some neighbourhoods, rely on electric medical equipment, concentrated in high-poverty areas, and survey results on outage preparedness. The Department publishes it on its Environment & Health Data Portal to inform residents and planners. Coverage is New York City, by neighbourhood, for the events named. Format and access: a public web page with charts, with related indicators in the portal's data explorer. Licence: not stated on the page; free to read. Caveats: the page notes some data have since been updated, and the excess-death analysis is summarised, not published as a dataset. It documents health impacts of electricity failure for cascading failure, emergency response and resilience models. A related catalogue record is the NYC 311 service requests, which log outage complaints.
